Mark a figure of fake data

Source: R/make_outputs.R
stamp_fake.Rd

stamp_fake() adds a large diagonal label "FAKE DATA" to a ggplot when make_outputs() calls the output function for a fake scenario. Otherwise it returns the figure as it is.

Usage

stamp_fake(q)

Arguments

q

A ggplot.

Value

q, with the label for a fake scenario.

Details

Call it in the figure code of the output function, before the figure is saved: q <- pbn::stamp_fake(q). For "real", and outside a call of make_outputs(), it returns q unchanged. The label is on each panel.

For a fake scenario, stamp_fake() needs the package ggplot2. It stops with an error when ggplot2 is not installed, and when q is not a ggplot.

See also

Other output: make_outputs()

Examples

# Outside make_outputs(), stamp_fake() returns the figure as it is.
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  q <- ggplot2::ggplot(data.frame(x = 1:3, y = 1:3), ggplot2::aes(x, y))
  identical(pbn::stamp_fake(q), q)
}
#> [1] TRUE
